concurrency: Terra coordinator, Sol owner, Astra adviser and up to three Luna scouts occupy six reasoning slots. Start Astra now because repeated reported misses and nonpublication create strategic uncertainty and an expensive wrong-turn risk; no screen is a prerequisite. Run S1, S2 and S4 initially; queue S3 and L7 in a reused scout slot. L5 and L6 reuse their conversations after dependencies and Sol review. Reserve a separate reviewer slot for any later artifact by releasing a completed conversation. No report proves any assignment ran. Future authorized runs use at most four processes, eight CPU cores and 16 GiB; serialize shared writers. No actual execution here.
reuse: Preserve all stable IDs and locked decisions; the Sol assignment E1 is distinct from external source E1. Reuse scout-c for S3 then L7, scout-b for L5 and scout-d for L6. Terra screens relevance and contradictions as available and retains original evidence and dissent for experts. Deadlines do not reset on reassignment.

expert_and_human_triggers.sol: Review measurement and any consequential algorithm or architectural choices before substantial dependent implementation; independent patch review before acceptance and ownership of consequential changes or exhausted repairs.
expert_and_human_triggers.astra: Consult now on the repeated reported misses/nonpublications and uncertain tradeoffs, without treating them as verified or making screening a prerequisite. Return actionable strategic alternatives and stop.
expert_and_human_triggers.human: Ask early about real operating conditions and tolerable delay/uncertainty, and seek authorization for any actual future campaign. Missing answers do not authorize changed targets or execution. Request available lab records only through an authorized channel.
expert_and_human_triggers.repair: Preserve original reports and any actual failures and causal evidence; allow at most one evidence-backed local worker repair, then escalate to Sol. Do not loosen gates, dates, phase, presence, END or payload requirements.

rejected_research: Claiming a fresh run, a root cause, a hardware limit or a preferred estimator from the summaries.
Estimating population rates from the small selected subset or treating final error at eight seconds as acquisition success at six seconds.
Pooling the two distinct reported sets or inferring every-publication coverage from final-summary data.
Broad undirected estimator searches, changing gates, or running a campaign during this paper exercise.
assumptions_and_uncertainties: E2 is a hypothetical second-operator report of a separate set: ten of twelve published by eight seconds; among those ten, median final error is 0.11 Hz, median reported uncertainty 0.06 Hz and three intervals missed. Two had no publication by ten seconds.

Raw captures and exact processing revision are unavailable; per-capture results, seed list, commands and audited timing definitions are missing. No reproduction or causal inference is possible from the summary alone.
The original six-second error and every-finite-interval targets remain in force; later windows are diagnostic and nonpublication must remain in denominators.
Source revision and dirty baseline remain packet claims; future execution requires authorization and provenance verification.
